title: Cologne Cathedral
note: Gothic cathedral whose twin spires reach about 157 m.

title: St Peter's Basilica
note: Vatican basilica with Michelangelo's dome, about 136 m to the cross.

title: Leaning Tower of Pisa
note: Campanile about 56 m high, famous for its tilt since construction.

title: Ivan the Great Bell Tower
note: Kremlin bell tower about 81 m high, long the tallest structure in Moscow.

title: Ulm Minster
note: Gothic church with the tallest church spire in the world, about 161.5 m.

title: Washington Monument
note: Marble obelisk about 169 m high in Washington DC.

title: CN Tower
note: Toronto communications tower, 553 m, once the tallest freestanding structure.

title: Gateway Arch
note: Stainless-steel arch 192 m high in St Louis.

title: Edzna Five-Story Building
note: Maya pyramid-palace about 31 m high in Campeche.

title: Hassan Tower, Rabat
note: Unfinished Almohad minaret, about 44 m of a planned 86 m.

title: Great Mosque of Agadez
note: Mud-brick minaret about 27 m high in the Sahel.

title: Colossi of Memnon
note: Pair of seated statues of Amenhotep III, about 18 m high.

title: Yingxian Wooden Pagoda
note: Liao-dynasty timber pagoda about 67 m high, the tallest wooden pagoda.

title: Songyue Pagoda
note: Brick pagoda about 40 m high, China's oldest surviving pagoda.

title: Toji Five-Storey Pagoda
note: Kyoto pagoda about 55 m high, the tallest wooden pagoda in Japan.

title: Tokyo Skytree
note: Broadcasting tower 634 m high, the tallest tower in the world.

title: Pha That Luang
note: Gilded stupa in Vientiane about 45 m high, national symbol of Laos.

title: Wat Arun
note: Bangkok temple with a central prang about 70 m high.

title: Charminar
note: Hyderabad monument with four minarets, about 56 m high.

title: Ruwanwelisaya
note: Anuradhapura stupa, originally about 103 m high.

title: Gommateshwara statue at Shravanabelagola
note: Monolithic Jain statue about 17.5 m high.

title: Vijay Stambha, Chittorgarh
note: Victory tower about 37 m high in Rajasthan.

title: Galata Tower
note: Genoese stone tower in Istanbul about 67 m high.

title: Azadi Tower
note: Tehran monument about 45 m high built for the 2,500-year celebration.

title: Tomb of Cyrus at Pasargadae
note: Limestone tomb of Cyrus the Great about 11 m high.

title: Alexander's campaign route from Granicus to the Hyphasis
note: Dated stops: Granicus 334 BCE, Issus 333, Gaugamela 331, Persepolis 330, Hydaspes 326.

title: Jianzhen's voyage to Japan
note: Chinese monk reached Japan on the sixth attempt after crossing from Yangzhou.

title: Ennin's travels in Tang China
note: Japanese monk diary records stops from Yangzhou to Mount Wutai and Chang'an.

title: Erik the Red's settlement of Greenland
note: Norse colonisation of Eastern and Western Settlements from Iceland.

title: Chola naval expedition to Srivijaya
note: Rajendra Chola's raid on Kedah and Srivijaya ports across the Bay of Bengal.

title: First Crusade march
note: Route from Clermont to Constantinople, Antioch (1098) and Jerusalem (1099).

title: Mongol western campaign of Batu
note: Mongol advance through Ryazan, Kiev (1240) and Hungary (1241).

title: Cortes's march to Tenochtitlan
note: Route from Veracruz via Tlaxcala and Cholula to Tenochtitlan.

title: Drake's circumnavigation
note: English voyage in the Golden Hind via Strait of Magellan and Moluccas, returning 1580.

title: Mendana's voyage to the Solomon Islands
note: Spanish expedition from Callao that reached Santa Isabel in 1568.

title: Nansen's Fram drift expedition
note: Ship frozen into Arctic ice in 1893, drifted to 85 degrees N before 1896.

title: Persian Royal Road
note: Achaemenid road from Sardis to Susa with Herodotus-recorded stations.

title: Gil Eanes's passage of Cape Bojador
note: Portuguese navigator rounded Cape Bojador in 1434 opening the African coast.

title: Hernando de Soto's expedition
note: Spanish expedition through Florida, Georgia, Alabama and reaching the Mississippi in 1541.

title: Tea Horse Road
note: Caravan route linking Yunnan and Sichuan tea regions with Tibet.

title: Matuyama-Brunhes geomagnetic reversal
note: Last full reversal of Earth's magnetic field.

title: Azolla event
note: Arctic freshwater fern blooms drew down CO2 and aided Cenozoic cooling.

title: Columbia River flood basalts
note: Large igneous province covering the Pacific Northwest.

title: Carboniferous rainforest collapse
note: Climate drying fragmented the coal-forest ecosystems of Pangaea.

title: Pongola glaciation
note: One of the oldest glacial deposits, in South Africa's Pongola Supergroup.

title: Barberton S2 spherule impact
note: Large asteroid impact preserved in South Africa's Barberton greenstone belt.

title: Francevillian biota
note: Gabon fossils interpreted as early large multicellular life.

title: Middle Eocene Climatic Optimum
note: Warming interval that interrupted Cenozoic cooling.

title: Oceanic Anoxic Event 1a
note: Early Aptian ocean oxygen collapse with black shale deposition.

title: Mid-Pleistocene Transition
note: Glacial cycles shifted from 41,000- to roughly 100,000-year periods.

title: Expansion of C4 grasslands
note: Spread of C4 grasses reshaped savanna ecosystems and herbivore evolution.

title: Lomagundi-Jatuli carbon isotope excursion
note: Major positive carbon isotope shift after the Great Oxidation.

title: Meltwater Pulse 1A
note: Rapid sea-level rise of about 14-18 m during deglaciation.

title: Chesapeake Bay impact crater
note: Late Eocene asteroid impact producing a buried crater about 40 km wide.

title: Gilboa fossil forest
note: Earliest known forest, preserved in New York State.

title: Hildegard of Bingen
note: German abbess, composer, visionary and writer on natural medicine.

title: Mary Wollstonecraft
note: Author of A Vindication of the Rights of Woman (1792).

title: Florence Nightingale
note: Founder of modern nursing, Crimean War reformer and statistician.

title: Joan of Arc
note: Peasant girl who led French forces and was burned in 1431.

title: Nefertiti
note: Great Royal Wife of Akhenaten, known from the Berlin bust.

title: Dihya al-Kahina
note: Berber queen who resisted the Umayyad conquest of the Maghreb.

title: Amina of Zazzau
note: Hausa warrior queen traditionally credited with city-wall building.

title: Nehanda Nyakasikana
note: Shona spirit medium and leader of the 1896 uprising.

title: Mekatilili wa Menza
note: Giriama woman who led resistance to British rule in Kenya.

title: Funmilayo Ransome-Kuti
note: Nigerian suffragist and anti-tax campaigner.

title: Sammu-ramat
note: Assyrian queen regent, basis of the Semiramis legend.

title: Aisha bint Abi Bakr
note: Wife of Muhammad and a major transmitter of hadith.

title: Sorghaghtani Beki
note: Mongol princess, mother of Mongke and Kublai Khan.

title: Lady Trieu
note: Vietnamese woman who led a revolt against Wu rule in 248.

title: Queen Suriyothai
note: Ayutthaya queen who died in battle in 1548 according to chronicles.

title: Ahilyabai Holkar
note: Maratha ruler of Malwa who rebuilt Hindu temples across India.

title: Begum Rokeya
note: Bengali writer and founder of a girls' school in Calcutta.

title: Qiu Jin
note: Chinese revolutionary and feminist executed in 1907.

title: Shin Saimdang
note: Joseon artist and calligrapher, mother of Yi I.

title: Higuchi Ichiyo
note: First prominent modern Japanese woman writer, died aged 24.

title: Mary Prince
note: Bermuda-born enslaved woman whose 1831 narrative aided abolition.

title: Zumbi dos Palmares
note: Leader of the Brazilian maroon state of Palmares, killed in 1695.

title: Mary Reibey
note: Convict who became a leading Sydney merchant.

title: Bennelong
note: Wangal man who mediated between Aboriginal people and the First Fleet.

title: Phillis Wheatley
note: Enslaved poet who published Poems on Various Subjects (1773).

title: Eratosthenes measures the Earth
note: Alexandria scholar estimated Earth's circumference from shadows at Syene.

title: Observation of the supernova of 1054
note: Chinese and Arab astronomers recorded the supernova that formed the Crab Nebula.

title: Tiangong Kaiwu
note: Song Yingxing's encyclopedia of Chinese technology.

title: On the Origin of Species
note: Darwin's publication of evolution by natural selection.

title: Eclipse of Thales
note: Solar eclipse of 585 BCE said to have been predicted by Thales.

title: Ebers Papyrus
note: Egyptian medical papyrus with over 700 remedies.

title: Hanaoka Seishu's general anaesthesia
note: Japanese surgeon operated under oral anaesthesia in 1804.

title: John Snow and the Broad Street cholera outbreak
note: Mapped cholera deaths to a water pump in Soho.

title: Discovery of insulin
note: Banting, Best, Collip and Macleod first used insulin on a diabetic patient in Toronto.

title: Antikythera mechanism
note: Ancient Greek geared astronomical calculator recovered from a shipwreck.

title: Al-Jazari's Book of Ingenious Mechanical Devices
note: Mechanical engineering treatise describing automata and water clocks.

title: Opening of the Tokaido Shinkansen
note: First high-speed railway, linking Tokyo and Osaka.

title: Canton system
note: Qing policy restricting foreign trade to Guangzhou.

title: Amazon rubber boom
note: Rubber extraction reshaped Manaus and caused indigenous exploitation.

title: Asian financial crisis
note: Currency collapse beginning with the Thai baht in July 1997.

title: Transmission of Buddhism to Japan
note: Baekje court sent Buddhist images and scriptures to Yamato Japan.

title: Babylonian captivity
note: Deportation of Judeans to Babylon after the destruction of Jerusalem in 586 BCE.

title: Francis Xavier's arrival in Japan
note: Jesuit mission landed at Kagoshima in 1549.

title: Nestorian Stele of Xi'an
note: Tang stele recording the arrival of Syriac Christianity in China.

title: Chauvet cave paintings
note: Ardeche cave with some of the earliest figurative paintings.

title: Negritude movement
note: Cesaire, Senghor and Damas launched a Black cultural movement in Paris.

title: Gandhara Buddhist art
note: Greco-Buddhist sculpture under the Kushans.

title: Shijing
note: Earliest Chinese poetry anthology of 305 poems.

title: Popol Vuh
note: K'iche' Maya creation narrative written in the 1550s.

title: Kebra Nagast
note: Ethiopian epic on Solomon, Sheba and the Ark of the Covenant.

title: Rig Veda
note: Oldest Vedic hymn collection composed in the Punjab.

title: Tale of Kieu
note: Nguyen Du's verse novel, the national epic of Vietnam.

title: Hurrian Hymn no. 6
note: Clay tablet from Ugarit bearing the oldest known notated song.

title: Birth of reggae
note: Jamaican genre popularised worldwide by Bob Marley and others.

title: Amir Khusrau
note: Poet and musician credited with developing qawwali.

title: Tang Code
note: Comprehensive legal code that shaped East Asian law.

title: Kouroukan Fouga charter
note: Mande constitutional charter attributed to Sundiata's assembly.

title: Mecelle
note: Ottoman civil code based on Islamic law.

title: Origins of the Mesoamerican ballgame
note: Earliest ballcourt at Paso de la Amada, Chiapas.

title: Cuju
note: Chinese ball game recorded in the Warring States and Han periods.

title: Abebe Bikila wins the Rome Olympic marathon
note: Ethiopian runner won barefoot, the first African Olympic marathon champion.

title: Chipko movement
note: Village protests hugging trees against logging in Uttarakhand.

title: Minamata disease
note: Mercury poisoning from industrial wastewater in Kumamoto.

title: Rio Earth Summit
note: UN conference that opened the climate and biodiversity conventions.

title: Execution of Ken Saro-Wiwa
note: Ogoni activist hanged after campaigning against oil pollution.
